summary: Round 5, prose only, no production logic and no wire change; no object-store request is added, moved or authorised anywhere in this diff, and the request-rate framing in the new prose stays correct throughout (the coalescing target is ONE WHOLE-OBJECT GET per (node, segment), never per run; M5.66's cell now prices directory-then-slice as at most two-against-one at K=1 and exactly one at the ~400-run share, which is the only pair that does not authorise runs-per-node scaling). ALL FIVE ROUND-4 FINDINGS ARE FIXED AND I VERIFIED EACH AGAINST THE BYTES: Decision (c) at :160-175 no longer cites (b) for a claim (b) refutes and now turns on 'no reader in the tree ISSUES one'; (b3) at :233-241 is repriced as one new SegmentReader entry point with the codec objection scoped to the slice-only form; doc 10 section 8's banner at :214-226 and doc 04's now say the same thing as the section 7 banner; the sweep table is 19 contiguous rows at :286-304 with the single-enumeration paragraph after it at :306; headerRangeEndInclusive is cited as the existence proof only, with SegmentKey.headerLenOf + SegmentFormat.PREAMBLE_BYTES as the reachable primitives (both verified public and in `format`); 5.4%, ADR-0043's Status quoting the stream figure, the test javadoc and the .as() message, and the MODELLED backlog cell are all as described. I RE-DERIVED THE PRICE INDEPENDENTLY AND IT HOLDS (7/129 = 5.43%, 11,200/206,400 = 5.43%, 11,200/8,388,608 = 0.1335%, 206,400/8,388,608 = 2.4605%, 0.1335/2.4605 = 5.43%, 40.4x; measured 6/128 = 4.69%). TWO THINGS BLOCK, AND BOTH ARE THE FAILURE MODE THIS ROUND WAS ASKED TO CHECK. First, the superseded claim survives in exactly one place the sweep could not grep: ADR-0043's amendment header wraps 'because no range / is expressible' across a line break, so the literal string does not match, and that header is the newest, highest-authority text in the file an ADR-0041 auditor opens first -- contradicted by ADR-0044:80 and by line 240 of its own file, both written in this commit. Second, and larger than any prose finding in this task: the round-4 correction that the bounded read is header-then-slice REFUTES the only justification left for keeping the fields. The header range IS preamble plus directory, RunEntry carries byteStart/byteLen for every run, SegmentReader.find(RunKey) resolves them, and ADR-0043:117 says so in the sentence ADR-0044 quotes -- 'Without them it must read the directory first to learn the same thing'. Once the codec objection forces the directory fetch, the event's copies are redundant for the very read they are kept to enable, and (b1) -- 'the closest call in this record' -- was rejected against a reason the record's own correction had already killed.

findings.title: ADR-0043's new amendment header states the retired claim as the REASON, and the line break is why the sweep missed it
findings.summary: :3-15, added by this commit, reads 'what they were said to buy -- "coalescing without a directory read", which needs a ranged GET -- is dead, because no range\nis expressible.' ADR-0044:80 is headed '"NO RANGE IS EXPRESSIBLE" IS TOO STRONG' and tables two ranges that ARE expressible; line 240 of this same file, also added by this commit, reads 'ADR-0044 later found the stronger form of this claim -- "no range is expressible" -- to be wrong'. So the file asserts the claim at line 5 and retires it at line 240, both in newly written text. The causal claim is also wrong on ADR-0044's own terms: :228-229 says what is dead in that justification is the 'skip the directory' half, since a bounded read must fetch the directory first -- not nameability. ⚠️ WHY THE PRE-ROUND SWEEP MISSED IT: 'because no range' ends line 5 and 'is expressible' begins line 6, so a grep for the literal phrase returns every other site and not this one; a grep that does match is `grep -Pzo 'no range\s+is expressible'` or a reflow before grepping. The sweep table at :286-304 has a row for ADR-0043 'Decision (b)' and no row for the Status block, so criterion 3's artifact does not cover the site either.
findings.failure_scenario: ADR-0041:114 defers security.md rule 3's range half and hands off through this record; ADR-0043's Status block is the first thing an auditor of that deferral, and M5.66's owner following criterion 4, reads -- AGENTS.md makes a later amendment win over the prose below it. They read that the justification died because no range can be expressed, conclude a consumer-side range is physically impossible, and take M5.66's removal arm: a format change against six golden files, both readers, both writers, the fakes and three ADRs under non-negotiable 8, chosen on a wording artifact this commit retires 235 lines lower in the same file. This is the identical shape that blocked rounds 1, 3 and 4 (a banner or Status line asserting a claim the record it cites retires), reproduced a fifth time inside the fix for it.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Status block, replace 'is dead, because no range is expressible' with the reason ADR-0044 actually gives: it is dead because the union cannot be a ranged GET and because a bounded read must fetch the directory FIRST, which is the 'without a directory read' half. Add a sweep-table row for 'docs/.../decisions/0043-...md Status block' so the site is enumerated, and note in the sweep paragraph that the pattern list must be grepped against reflowed text -- line wrapping is what hid this one.

findings.title: Decision (b)'s surviving justification is refuted by Decision (b)'s own round-4 correction: the directory the bounded read must fetch already carries byteStart/byteLen
findings.summary: :102-104 is the whole reason the fields stay: 'they are the only thing that makes a bounded read possible later'. :91-96, added this round, establishes that the bounded read is TWO requests -- '[0, PREAMBLE + headerLen) -- preamble PLUS DIRECTORY' then the slice -- and that the slice-only one-request form is ruled out because 'u32 codecFlags lives per run in the DIRECTORY', so 'a reader that fetched the header HAS the directory'. But the directory is where the run's byte extent already lives: format/src/main/java/binjava/format/RunEntry.java:19 declares `RunEntry(RunKey key, int recordCount, long byteStart, int byteLen, ...)`, its javadoc says 'a consumer resolves its byte range' from it 'WITHOUT touching the run's bytes', and SegmentReader.find(RunKey) (format/src/main/java/binjava/format/SegmentReader.java:112) binary-searches it. A reader that has fetched the header therefore already holds byteStart/byteLen for its run and never needs the event's copies. ADR-0043:117 -- the sentence ADR-0044 quotes as the dead justification -- says it outright: 'Without them it must read the directory first to learn THE SAME THING.' Under the design ADR-0044 now specifies, it reads the directory first regardless. Nothing in the record addresses this: the sweep table at :286 dispositions `RunEntry.java` and `SegmentReader.java` as 'Not this question -- the segment directory's own coordinates', which is the same false 'confirmed' round 2 measured on doc 13, except here the directory's copy IS the question, because it is what makes the event's copy redundant. (b1), removal, is rejected at :217-221 as 'the closest call in this record' against a reason that does not survive the correction. What DOES survive is narrower and is not written down anywhere: the event's copies let a consumer issue the slice GET without waiting for the header round trip -- a latency argument, not a possibility one -- and 5.4% of the subscription stream may or may not be worth one RTT.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.66's owner takes criterion 2's first arm and builds the two-request reader the ADR authorises. They fetch [0, PREAMBLE + headerLen), call SegmentReader.find(key), and have the slice bounds in hand -- at which point criterion 2's requirement of 'a consumer that uses the EVENT's coordinates to drive it' forces them to prefer the wire copy over the directory entry the segment itself is authoritative for. That is two sources of truth for one run's extent with no cross-check: a writer that ever emits an event whose coordinates disagree with the directory (a repacked segment, an off-by-one in the publisher, a v3 event replayed against a rewritten object) produces a silent short or out-of-bounds slice instead of a directory lookup that would have been right. And independently of M5.66, VERSION_3 permanently carries 7 bytes per event whose recorded reason is false, with removal -- the option this record calls the closest call -- rejected against it; anyone re-pricing the field later reads a justification the same document's own correction destroys, which is exactly the 'justification that outlived the thing justifying it' defect (b2) at :227-231 is rejected for.
findings.suggested_fix: Either state the justification that survives -- the coordinates let the slice GET be issued without waiting for the header round trip, so the bounded read is one RTT rather than two, and price 5.4% of the subscription stream against that -- or re-take (b1) now that its opponent is gone. Whichever way, add a row to the sweep table for RunEntry/SegmentReader's directory copy as 'this question after all: the directory supplies the same extent to any reader that fetched the header', and make M5.66's criterion 2 say which of the two copies the reader is required to trust and assert they agree.

findings.title: M5.45f's done-cell says 'ADR-0044 derives that once and this cell does not re-derive it' twice, in one sentence
findings.summary: The cell reads '... at a MODELLED 7 bytes per event -- ADR-0044 derives that once and this cell deliberately does not re-derive it -- **5.4% of the subscription stream** and 0.134% of the segment -- ADR-0044 derives it ONCE and this cell does not re-derive it, because three rounds went on copies of the figure disagreeing with each other.' The same clause appears twice around the figures it brackets, which reads as a merge artifact from the round-4 edit.
findings.failure_scenario: No behaviour and no number is wrong. A status reader or the milestone review quotes this cell verbatim and the stutter reads as an unfinished edit in the one row that records how the number was settled. Lands under rule 11; fixing it is permitted and usually wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the second occurrence, keeping the 'because three rounds went on copies of the figure disagreeing with each other' tail on the first.
